note: D12 perf gate — maxMedian is the ceiling the gate compares each metric's p10 against (the key name predates the estimator change; the numbers are what matters). POLICY, alpha72: floor = 2x the measured p10, never raised without an argument in the commit, lowered whenever a metric gets faster. 2x, not the old >=2x-of-median, because the estimator changed: a median on a shared machine spread 30% across three runs of the same build, so the headroom had to absorb the measurement rather than the hardware. p10 is stable to ~7%, which leaves 2x to cover a slower CI box and nothing else. Before this, every floor sat 2.4-7.3x above its number and the gate had been gating nothing — which is how proxy-array-10k drifted 30 -> 55 ms unremarked. `check:bench` now reports that slack instead of hiding it.

measured-2026-08-18.note: up from 30.2: array read methods now hand back LIVE element proxies (writes through map()/filter() results land — the alpha61 silent-drop fix), so each element access is a real tracked read instead of a detached clone. Correctness bought with ~20ms on this 10k micro-op; maxMedian 75 unchanged and holding with headroom.

measured-2026-08-29.note: p10, on the alpha72 tree, after the live-proxy allocation fix (the child path is built on a cache MISS only, and the per-element key prefix is hoisted): a read method over a 10k array no longer allocates ten thousand arrays to look ten thousand entries up in a Map. Measured A/B over three runs each: baseline min 50.1-52.6 ms, after 46.6-49.9 ms.

measured-2026-09-20.note: NEW metric overlay-write-loop-10k: one async sweep that reads and writes every key of a 10k-key map. Added with the incremental read-your-writes overlay (a field report measured the quadratic version at 70.7 s of structuredClone inside a 150 s profile). Measured p10 47.96 ms on this tree, 19 200 ms before the fix — ~400x. Floor 96 = 2x p10, per the policy above.

measured-2026-09-23.note: NEW metrics ssr-provider-stream-10k / ssr-provider-ttfb: a 10k-node page under a root Provider, streamed (p10 of three runs: 22.2-23.0 ms; first chunk 0.012-0.015 ms, where the Fragment-buffering writer took ~18 ms). stream-10k floor = 2x p10. ttfb floor 1 ms, NOT 2x: 2x of 0.015 ms is timer noise on a slower box, while the regression it guards is ~1000x (a buffered Fragment waits for the whole page) — 1 ms catches that with room on any machine. NEW metric ssr-fragment-nest-ratio: 60 nested Fragments timed against the same chain of <span>s in one sample (best of 3 each), so the floor is machine-independent and TIGHT, not 2x: p10 0.74-0.80 across five runs, floor 1.0 (~1.3x). Planted and measured: the helper-generator Fragment writer (+60% absolute) reads 1.31; a CPU plant in the Fragment branch costing +40% absolute (1.07 -> 1.50 ms) reads 1.06-1.10 in three of three runs; both trip. A +15% plant reads 0.92 and passes. For the record, 1.0.9's buffered Fragment measures ~1.1 on this ratio and 1.45-1.50 ms absolute, the inlined streamed one 1.00-1.05 ms.
